title: Autonomic verification lane for batching & caching rollout with operator attestation
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Problem: Optimize suggests batching/caching profiles that reduce per-token cost but may risk tail latency regressions or subtle correctness changes. We need a safe, operator-attested path to auto-apply low-risk suggestions while providing a fast rollback and clear evidence for operators.

Proposal: Build an "autonomic verification lane" (AVL) — a sandboxed, short-lived deployment lane that can accept a suggestion, run it against replayed and sampled traffic, compute statistical deltas across latency/cost/quality signals, and produce a signed attestation package. The AVL integrates with the Optimize suggestions stream, Console approval flows, and our rollout controller to enable a gated auto-apply backed by quantitative checks and optional human attestation.

Key behaviors: 1) Shadow application: suggestions are applied in a shadow cluster that receives a sampled mirror (1-5%) of live requests and a deterministic replay of recent traffic for reproducibility. 2) Dual telemetry: compare baseline vs suggestion across p50/p95/p99 latency, per-request token cost, error rate, and a correctness score from a small eval prompt set. 3) Statistical gating: require configurable delta thresholds (e.g., latency p95 within +5ms or +3%) and Bayesian/bootstrapped confidence intervals for cost savings. 4) Attestation token: if checks pass, generate an attestation JSON signed by the AVL service; optionally require operator attestation (one or quorum) before promoting. 5) Rollout choreography: support staged promotion percentages, time windows, and automatic circuit-breaker rollback if live telemetry crosses cancel thresholds. 6) Audit trail: persist attestation, test artifacts, and telemetry snapshots for Console display and compliance audits.

Why different from existing flows: instead of only canary-ing in production or requiring manual operator steps, the AVL provides an evidence-first, replayable verification artifact that decouples the evaluation workload from production capacity and standardizes operator approvals across Optimize suggestions. It also provides machine-verifiable attestations that can be consumed by downstream automation (e.g., automatic commit after N operator attestations).
acceptance_criteria: AVL can ingest an Optimize suggestion and instantiate a sandboxed deployment that applies the suggested batching or kvcache profile
AVL can mirror sampled live traffic (configurable sample rate) and run deterministic replay for at least 10k recent requests
System computes baseline vs suggestion metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per request, 5 defined correctness evals) and stores a snapshot
Statistical gating engine evaluates deltas and outputs pass/fail with confidence scores using bootstrapped intervals
Attestation package produced on pass, signed by service key and viewable in Console with links to telemetry snapshots and replay logs
Operator attestation flow integrated into Console: single-approve or quorum approve options, with timestamps and operator IDs recorded
Rollout controller consumes attestation and can promote suggestion to staged rollout with percentage ramps and circuit-breaker thresholds
Automatic rollback triggers when live telemetry violates configured safety thresholds (e.g., p95 > baseline + 10% or error rate doubles), with rollback executed within 2 minutes of trigger
End-to-end tests (integration) covering success path, fail path, operator approval, and automatic rollback are present in ci/avl-tests
Documentation (Console guide + runbook) published and linked from Optimize suggestion UI
